question: Which organ in the urinary system is injured most often during trauma?
explanation: The kidney is the most frequently injured upper urinary tract organ because of its position and major blood supply. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T10#GNS213_U4_T10_h1)

question: Why do pelvic fractures often lead to lower urinary tract trauma?

options.A: The pelvis stores the main blood supply for the kidneys
options.B: The bony pelvis closely encases the bladder and urethra
options.C: Pelvic bones produce sharp bone fragments that dissolve tissue
options.D: Fractures cut off all nerve supply to the lower abdomen

explanation: Because the pelvic bones sit right next to the bladder and urethra, bone displacement during a fracture can easily damage these structures. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T10#GNS213_U4_T10_h1)

question: A gunshot wound to the abdomen is an example of what type of trauma?
explanation: Penetrating trauma happens when an object like a bullet or knife breaks through the skin and internal tissues. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T10#GNS213_U4_T10_h2)

question: A patient in a high-speed car crash is at high risk for which type of internal injury?

options.A: Localized inflammation from chronic urinary tract infection
options.B: Clean surgical cuts along the lining of the bladder
options.C: Superficial scratches on the external perineal skin
options.D: Rapid deceleration shearing forces on the renal pedicle

explanation: Sudden stopping in high-speed crashes creates pulling forces that can tear the main blood vessels attached to the kidneys. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T10#GNS213_U4_T10_h2)

question: A completely shattered kidney with torn main blood vessels is classified as which injury grade?
explanation: Grade V is the most severe level of kidney injury, involving a shattered organ or completely torn blood vessels. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T10#GNS213_U4_T10_h3)

question: What separates a Grade IV kidney injury from lesser grades?

options.A: Superficial cortical tearing less than one centimeter in depth
options.B: Presence of a simple contusion confined to the outer capsule
options.C: Complete separation of the kidney from the adrenal gland
options.D: Involvement of the renal collecting system or major blood vessels

explanation: Grade IV injuries reach deeper into the kidney's urine-collecting system or involve bleeding from major renal blood vessels. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T10#GNS213_U4_T10_h3)

question: What is a classic sign of a posterior urethral injury in male patients?
explanation: Seeing blood at the urethral opening is a strong warning sign of damage somewhere along the urinary tract. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T10#GNS213_U4_T10_h4)

question: A patient with a pelvic fracture has blood at the meatus and cannot urinate. What is the correct nursing action?

options.A: Insert a rigid latex urinary catheter immediately to drain the bladder
options.B: Encourage oral fluid intake until spontaneous voiding occurs
options.C: Withhold catheterization and report findings for a retrograde urethrogram
options.D: Perform digital rectal examination to force the prostate downward

explanation: Passing a catheter blindly can worsen a urethral tear, so imaging studies must be done first to check the area. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T10#GNS213_U4_T10_h4)

question: What physical sign is typical of a penile fracture?

options.A: Inability to feel lower extremity pulses

explanation: Tearing of the internal tissues causes severe bleeding under the skin, giving the penis a swollen, dark appearance. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T10#GNS213_U4_T10_h5)

question: Why is immediate surgery necessary for a suspected testicular rupture?

options.A: To prevent the development of permanent lower limb paralysis
options.B: To preserve testicular viability and long-term endocrine function
options.C: To eliminate the need for any postoperative pain medication
options.D: To stop immediate bleeding into the peritoneal cavity

explanation: Early surgical repair prevents tissue death and protects the testicle's ability to produce hormones and sperm. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T10#GNS213_U4_T10_h5)

question: What imaging test is best for evaluating a stable patient with a kidney injury?
explanation: A CT scan with contrast gives clear, detailed pictures of kidney damage, bleeding, and urine leaks. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T10#GNS213_U4_T10_h6)

question: What does blood in the urine (hematuria) usually indicate during a trauma assessment?

options.B: Definite destruction of the urinary bladder dome
options.C: Severe infection present prior to the trauma event
options.D: Possible injury anywhere along the urinary tract

explanation: Hematuria simply signals that trauma has affected some part of the urinary system, from the kidneys down to the urethra. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T10#GNS213_U4_T10_h6)

question: What is the main goal of conservative management for minor kidney injuries?

options.A: Allowing natural healing while monitoring closely for complications
options.B: Forcing rapid diuresis to flush out blood clots from the bladder
options.C: Preventing the patient from moving out of the hospital bed for weeks
options.D: Ensuring immediate surgical removal of the damaged kidney

explanation: Most minor kidney bruises and cuts heal on their own with supportive care and close observation. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T10#GNS213_U4_T10_h7)

question: A patient resting with a mild kidney injury develops a fast heart rate and falling blood pressure. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Encourage the patient to get out of bed to stimulate circulation
options.B: Notify the surgical team immediately for signs of ongoing bleeding
options.C: Administer oral sleeping pills to help the patient rest quietly
options.D: Decrease intravenous fluid infusion rates to prevent fluid overload

explanation: Dropping blood pressure and a fast pulse can mean internal bleeding is getting worse, requiring urgent medical review. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T10#GNS213_U4_T10_h7)

question: What is the main purpose of a suprapubic catheter placed during bladder surgery?

options.A: To divert urine away from the bladder repair site
options.B: To deliver concentrated antibiotics directly to the kidneys
options.C: To allow the patient to walk immediately without a bag
options.D: To measure accurate intra-abdominal pressure hourly

explanation: A suprapubic catheter drains urine directly through the lower abdomen, keeping the healing bladder empty and free from tension. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T10#GNS213_U4_T10_h8)

question: Why is keeping a urinary catheter clear and open so important after urinary surgery?

options.A: Continuous high pressure prevents the formation of normal scar tissue
options.B: Blocked catheters automatically cause permanent kidney failure within minutes
options.C: Urine must back up into the renal pelvis to lubricate internal tissue
options.D: Clots and kinks cause bladder spasms and strain surgical suture lines

explanation: Clear drainage prevents urine buildup and painful spasms that could pull apart fresh surgical stitches. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T10#GNS213_U4_T10_h8)

question: What long-term complication can develop from kidney scarring after trauma?
explanation: Kidney scarring can reduce blood flow inside the organ, activating hormone pathways that lead to high blood pressure later on. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T10#GNS213_U4_T10_h9)

question: A patient treated for a urethral injury returns months later reporting a weak urine stream. What is the most likely cause?
explanation: As the urethra heals, scar tissue can form and narrow the passage, leading to a weak urine stream and straining. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T10#GNS213_U4_T10_h9)
